title: Inference Fleet Ops Command Deck — Dedicated Capacity Health & Burst Controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, action-oriented command deck for dedicated inference fleets that surfaces health signals across GPU nodes, cost impact of burst/autoscale actions, and fast controls for on-call engineers. This UX focuses on a fleet-level view (multiple pools) and a focused pool inspector panel. Deliverables: 1) high-fidelity Figma prototypes for desktop (two breakpoints), 2) interactive burst schedule editor, 3) cost delta estimator integrated into control modals, 4) component spec for telemetry sparklines and alert badges. Goal: reduce time-to-action when pools approach SLO thresholds and give product teams confidence to tune autoscale/burst settings without deep infra knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows fleet overview + drill-down pool inspector with health banding and top-3 alerts
Burst editor prototype allows scheduling one-off bursts, recurring windows, and immediate apply with confirmation modal
Cost estimator displays per-hour and projected-24h delta before action is applied
Controls include safe-guards: canary burst, rollback button, and quick links to relevant runbook entries
Component tokens and spacing follow Console design system and have annotated specs for engineering handoff
design_notes: Primary layout: left column = fleet list with compact health strip and cost score; center = selected pool timeline + KPIs (avg latency, 95th, queued requests, GPU util); right = action rail with 'Scale', 'Burst', 'Pause', 'Drill into nodes'. Health strip uses stacked signals: infra (node loss), runtime (OOM/evictions), performance (p95 breaching), and cost anomaly. We propose an inline cost estimator exposed via an info icon; defaults to conservative estimates using current quantization and batching profiles. Interaction states include canary toggle and 'simulated impact' preview that overlays KPIs for the 60m window after change. Accessibility: keyboard flows for action rail and ARIA labels for status chips.
review_feedback: Marco Chen (Eng): Add a non-blocking simulation mode that runs an offline capacity check before allowing immediate apply (suggested ENG-50712).
Priya Singh (PM): Cost estimator must show both host-hour and tokenized cost deltas; avoid hiding the cumulative 24h number behind tooltips.
Samir Rao (SRE): Health banding thresholds should be configurable per-customer; add a compact 'incident timeline' row to correlate SLO breaches to recent deploys.
Design critique (10/08): Narrow breakpoint needs tighter stacking for action rail; consider collapsing KPIs into a popover to save vertical space.
decisions: Use a three-band health visualization (green/yellow/red) supplemented by micro-alert badges for exact signals
Expose burst controls at both fleet and pool levels — fleet-level burst applies to selected pools only
Ship cost estimator as read-only at launch; enable editable assumptions in a follow-up (Console-2026.02)
Canary burst = default ON for enterprise customers; toggle persisted per-org

ux_risks: Users may misinterpret cost estimator leading to accidental expensive bursts — mitigation: strong modal confirmation and simulated impact preview
Autoscale controls could be used reactively during incidents and cause oscillations — mitigation: canary bursts + recommended guardrails in UI
Too many signals in fleet view could overwhelm new users — mitigation: progressive disclosure and 'compact' density option
